verified.flags: BIO_WORKINGSET12 is below BVEC_POOL_OFFSET13; existing bits1..11 and pool13..15 unchanged. bio_reset retains only bits>=13, so it clears WORKINGSET on reuse. Header rejects future overlap.
verified.tagging: __bio_add_page tags a newly added page only when PageWorkingset. In this MM stage only previously active file-cache pages receive this flag. Newly allocated anonymous pages and new swapin pages are not tagged.
verified.same_page_merge: 4.19 __bio_try_merge_page accepts only the same struct page and contiguous offset; that page was tagged during its initial vector insertion. It cannot merge a different hot page unnoticed.
verified.submission: submit_bio only enables memory stall for BIO_WORKINGSET and bio_has_data and non-write operations. Enter and leave use a local nested-state snapshot around generic_make_request; no intervening local early return or access to bio after potential completion/free.
verified.operation_scope: The condition follows upstream read-direction logic (!op_is_write), not equality with REQ_OP_READ. PC/passthrough constructors bio_add_pc_page do not tag WORKINGSET in the audited code.
verified.throttle: blkcg returns on zero delay before entering. use_memdelay alone gates enter/leave; timeout and fatal-signal paths both pass through io_schedule_finish and psi_memstall_leave. Existing250ms cap is preserved.
verified.clones: __bio_clone_fast and bio_split do not copy WORKINGSET, matching pinned5.15. Normal synchronous block stacking and queue splits are processed within the original generic_make_request invocation and remain inside its parent memstall interval. No mandatory clone propagation change was identified.
verified.direct_io: fs/block_dev and iomap direct IO use bio_iov_iter_get_pages, which fills bvecs directly rather than calling __bio_add_page; ordinary directIO is not misrepresented as file-cache refault. Legacy fs/direct-io uses bio_add_page; ordinary anonymous user buffers still lack PageWorkingset.

limits: An unusual legacy directIO read into an already-uptodate file-backed mmap buffer carrying PageWorkingset can inherit upstream tagging despite not representing a cache refault. Not newly introduced relative to the selected upstream algorithm; a strict !PageUptodate tagging filter would be a further semantic change needing its own test.

A newly cloned bio handed to another task before its first top-level submit can lose the hint. The audited normal stack does not require clone-copy to count its caller submission interval; do not claim all arbitrary out-of-tree asynchronous clone users are covered.
bio_add_pc_page/passthrough and direct_make_request do not receive this new submit hook by construction; generic userspace directIO is IO pressure, not inherently memory pressure.
Swap/frontswap/zram MEM classification remains intentionally deferred until coherent anonymous workingset detection; IO pressure and pre-existing reclaim PSI still exist.
decision: No source changes from this review. Keep current upstream-equivalent block hooks and root-run validation; record unusual DIO/async-clone boundaries instead of claiming universal coverage.
